q-96324.name: Question 1
q-96324.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the Pythagorean identity 

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x=1.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic Pythagorean identity

$$
{cosh}^{2}⁡x-{sinh}^{2}⁡x=1.
$$

Using the above, we rewrite and calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{1-{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{1-(1+{sinh}^{2}⁡x)}\text{d}x \\  & =-\int \frac{1}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\int {csch}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{coth}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

q-96307.name: Question 2
q-96307.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the Pythagorean identity 

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x=1.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic Pythagorean identity

$$
{cosh}^{2}⁡x-{sinh}^{2}⁡x=1.
$$

Additionally, we have

$$
\operatorname{sech}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}
$$

Using the above, we rewrite the denominator and calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (1-{sinh}^{2}⁡x{sech}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (1-{sinh}^{2}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{{cosh}^{2}⁡x-{sinh}^{2}⁡x}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {sech}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{tanh}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

q-348024.name: Question 9
q-348024.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the secant-tangent identity 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic secant-tangent identity

$$
1-{tanh}^{2}⁡x={sech}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we rewrite the integral and evaluate it, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\frac{8\operatorname{sinh}⁡x-8\operatorname{sinh}⁡x{tanh}^{2}⁡x}{{sech}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\frac{8\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\cdot (1-{tanh}^{2}⁡x)}{{sech}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\frac{8\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\cdot {sech}^{2}⁡x}{{sech}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}8\operatorname{sinh}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =8\operatorname{cosh}⁡x{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =8(\operatorname{cosh}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)-\operatorname{cosh}⁡0) \\  & =8(\frac{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡2}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{0}+{e}^{-(0)}}{2}) \\  & =8(\frac{2+{2}^{-1}}{2}-1) \\  & =8(\frac{5}{4}-1) \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

q-96413.name: Question 10
q-96413.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the secant-tangent identity 

$$
{sec}^{2}⁡x-1={tan}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic secant-tangent identity

$$
1-{sech}^{2}⁡x={tanh}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we rewrite the integral and evaluate it, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{{sech}^{2}⁡x}{1-{sech}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{{sech}^{2}⁡x}{{tanh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\cdot \frac{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\frac{1}{{sinh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{csch}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{coth}⁡x\,{|}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =-\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)+\operatorname{coth}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+1}{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-1}+\frac{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+1}{{e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-1} \\  & =-\frac{{3}^{2}+1}{{3}^{2}-1}+\frac{{2}^{2}+1}{{2}^{2}-1} \\  & =-\frac{5}{4}+\frac{5}{3} \\  & =\frac{5}{12}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

q-348041.worked_solution:

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic identity

$$
1+{csch}^{2}⁡x={coth}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we rewrite the integral and evaluate it, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡8}\frac{1+{csch}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sech}⁡x{coth}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡8}\frac{{coth}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sech}⁡x{coth}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡8}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sech}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡8}\operatorname{cosh}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sinh}⁡x{|}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡8} \\  & =\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡8)-\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡8}-{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡8}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{8-{8}^{-1}}{2}-\frac{2-{2}^{-1}}{2} \\  & =\frac{63}{16}-\frac{3}{4} \\  & =\frac{51}{16}\end{aligned}
$$

q-165895.name: Question 16
q-165895.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the Pythagorean identity

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic Pythagorean identity

$$
{cosh}^{2}⁡\theta -{sinh}^{2}⁡\theta =1.
$$

Setting $\theta =3x+2,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{cosh}^{2}⁡(3x+2)-{sinh}^{2}⁡(3x+2) & =1 \\ 1+{sinh}^{2}⁡(3x+2) & ={cosh}^{2}⁡(3x+2).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{6}{1+{sinh}^{2}⁡(3x+2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{6}{{cosh}^{2}⁡(3x+2)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =6\int \frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡(3x+2)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =6\int {sech}^{2}⁡(3x+2)\,\text{d}x \\  & =6\cdot \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{tanh}⁡(3x+2)+C \\  & =2\operatorname{tanh}⁡(3x+2)+C\end{aligned}
$$

q-96522.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the cosecant-cotangent identity 

$$
1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic cosecant-cotangent identity

$$
{coth}^{2}⁡\theta -1={csch}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Setting $\theta =7x-2,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{coth}^{2}⁡(7x-2)-1 & ={csch}^{2}⁡(7x-2) \\ {coth}^{2}⁡(7x-2) & ={csch}^{2}⁡(7x-2)+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{csch}^{3}⁡(7x-2)+\operatorname{csch}⁡(7x-2)}{\operatorname{coth}⁡(7x-2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡(7x-2)[{csch}^{2}⁡(7x-2)+1]}{\operatorname{coth}⁡(7x-2)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡(7x-2){coth}^{2}⁡(7x-2)}{\operatorname{coth}⁡(7x-2)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \operatorname{csch}⁡(7x-2)\operatorname{coth}⁡(7x-2)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{7}\operatorname{csch}⁡(7x-2)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

q-165894.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the Pythagorean identity

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the hyperbolic Pythagorean identity

$$
{cosh}^{2}⁡\theta -{sinh}^{2}⁡\theta =1.
$$

Setting $\theta =2x,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{cosh}^{2}⁡(2x)-{sinh}^{2}⁡(2x) & =1 \\ 1+{sinh}^{2}⁡(2x) & ={cosh}^{2}⁡(2x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2+2{sinh}^{2}⁡(2x)}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(2x)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{2(1+{sinh}^{2}⁡(2x))}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(2x)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2{cosh}^{2}⁡(2x)}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(2x)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \operatorname{cosh}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡(2x)+C \\  & =\operatorname{sinh}⁡(2x)+C\end{aligned}
$$
